input: Negotiate the renewal terms on my office lease

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which specific terms are on the table (rent, lease length, break clauses, fit-out allowances, etc.) determines where to focus negotiation energy and which levers to pull.
The current lease expiry date and how much time is left before it expires sets the urgency and negotiating timeline — too close to expiry and leverage is reduced.
Whether the user is negotiating directly with the landlord, through a broker, or with a property manager changes the communication strategy and who needs to be involved in the plan.
Budget limits for rent or one-time costs set hard boundaries on what acceptable terms look like and when to walk away.
Understanding the user's priority — e.g., lowest rent vs. longest term vs. flexibility to exit — shapes which concessions to push for and which to trade away.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like (specific rent reduction, added perks, a break clause) defines the target and helps measure whether the negotiation succeeded.
Knowing what support the user needs right now — a negotiation script, a comparison of market rates, a checklist of clauses to review — determines the immediate next action.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to negotiate the renewal terms of their office lease, likely aiming for better conditions than what is currently offered or in place.

questions.title: Which specific lease terms are you trying to change?
questions.description: Identify the exact terms in scope for negotiation — rent amount, lease duration, break clauses, rent-free periods, fit-out contributions, or others.

questions.title: When does your current lease expire?
questions.description: Establish the lease expiry date and how much runway remains, as this directly affects negotiating leverage and the urgency of the plan.

questions.title: Are you negotiating directly with the landlord yourself?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is the sole negotiator or if a broker, lawyer, or property manager is involved, which shapes the communication and preparation strategy.

questions.title: What is the maximum rent or cost you can accept?
questions.description: Identify the hard budget ceiling for rent or any one-time costs such as deposits or fit-out expenses, to define the walk-away point.

questions.title: What matters most — lower rent, flexibility, or lease length?
questions.description: Understand the user's top priority among common negotiation outcomes so the plan focuses on the right concessions and trade-offs.

questions.title: What does a successful renewal outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Define the concrete target result — e.g., a specific rent reduction percentage, a break clause at year 2, a rent-free fit-out period — to set a clear goal.

questions.title: What kind of help do you need to get started right now?
questions.description: Identify the immediate deliverable the user needs — a negotiation script, market rate research, a clause checklist, or a step-by-step action plan.
